newsitem.title: GERMANY: German deputy urges Iran to lift death sentences.
newsitem.headline: German deputy urges Iran to lift death sentences.

text.p: A German member of parliament appealed to Iran on Monday not to execute four members of the Bahai faith who have been sentenced to death for their religious beliefs.

Ruprecht Polenz, an Iranian affairs specialist in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union, said he had sent letters of protest to the Iranian justice and foreign ministries and to Iran's ambassador in Germany.
"Execution is imminent for two of the men. Two others are waiting for a decision from Iran's highest court," said Polenz.
The two men in most imminent danger -- Musa Talibi and Zabiullah Mahrami -- were convicted separately last year of "apostasy", a term used to denote abandoning Islam.
The United States appealed last week for their death sentences to be lifted after they were confirmed by the Iranian supreme court.
Talibi and Mahrami were moved to a new prison, raising fears that their execution could be carried out soon, the German branch of the faith said in a statement.
The German branch said a total of 12 Bahais were in custody in Iran because of their religious beliefs.

The Bahai faith, an offshoot of Islam, was created in Iran 150 years ago. It claims six million members worldwide, including 300,000 in Iran where it is officially considered "a misleading and wayward sect".
Bahais say more than 200 members of their faith have been executed in Iran for their religious beliefs since the Islamic revolution in 1979.
